# NL2SQL-BUGs: A Benchmark for Detecting Semantic Errors in NL2SQL Translation

[All reading notes](../reading-notes.md) · [Catalog entry](../README.md#nl2sql-bugs)

**Full paper read · 2026-11-09**

[Original source](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2503.11984v2) · arXiv:2503.11984v2, 15 June 2025, author KDD 2025 manuscript

**Reading coverage:** All twelve PDF pages, Sections 1-7 and Appendices A-B, 31-subtype taxonomy, annotation protocol, all result tables and worked SQL cases.

## Research question

Executable SQL can be wrong relative to a natural-language request, and detecting the error class is harder than judging a query as wrong.

## Method

The authors screen BIRD reference questions/SQL, generate candidates with RESDSQL, CodeS and CHESS, deduplicate SQL, then annotate incorrect queries using a nine-category/31-subtype taxonomy. Two SQL experts label types, with third-expert adjudication.

## Evaluation

The 2,018 instances comprise 1,019 labeled correct and 999 incorrect candidates. Six LLMs perform binary correctness and multi-label type detection. Correctness labeling primarily compares execution results with screened reference SQL; subtype evaluation uses the fraction of true instances whose label is found.

## What the results support

Binary accuracy is around three quarters while type identification is substantially weaker. The paper also reports manually validated candidate reference errors in Spider and BIRD.

## Limits and qualifications

The stated semantic task includes errors hidden by current-instance agreement, but result-based labels can miss those cases. Type-Specific Accuracy is recall-like and does not itself penalize extra predicted types. Generator mix, selected BIRD references and expert labeling conventions limit transfer.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

A benchmark for candidate-SQL verifiers and error explanations, separate from deciding whether the original request is answerable.

## Checks against the paper

These are interpretations checked against the source, not verbatim quotations attributed to its authors.

| Claim or inference examined | Original evidence | Location | Assessment |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Type-Specific Accuracy is classification accuracy. | The Section 5.3 formula divides correctly found type labels by all instances truly containing that type, without a false-positive denominator. | Section 5.3, TSA formula; Table 2 | Describe as per-type recall-like coverage, not ordinary overall accuracy. |
| Correct labels establish universal semantic correctness. | Section 2 includes current-instance accidental agreement as an error, but Section 4.2 assigns correctness primarily through execution-result matching. | Sections 2.1 and 4.2 | Retain the instance/reference-bound labeling limitation. |
